examples.label: Take ownership of the SYSTEM-run service binary
Start the service to run it as SYSTEM

notes:
=== Hyper-V Administrators — Virtual DC Compromise ===
Hyper-V Admins get full Hyper-V access — if DCs are virtualized, this equals Domain Admin.

=== PRIMARY ATTACK PATH — Cloning Virtual DC ===
1. Export/clone a running DC VM to accessible share or local path
2. Mount the .vhdx offline (no domain authentication needed)
3. Access E:\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit + C:\Windows\System32\config\SYSTEM offline
4. Run secretsdump.py → all domain hashes without touching the live domain

No exploitation needed — management rights = unrestricted VM access.
No alerts against live domain — reading a static disk image is invisible to AD logging.

=== SECONDARY PATH — Hard Link Privilege Escalation ===
Targets vmms.exe behavior when deleting a VM:
vmms.exe runs as SYSTEM and restores permissions on .vhdx file without impersonating the deleting user.

Chain:
1. Run hyperv-eop.ps1 → creates hard link: .vhdx path redirects to maintenanceservice.exe
2. Delete the VM → SYSTEM's permission restoration redirects to maintenanceservice.exe
3. Current user now has Full Control over maintenanceservice.exe (in Program Files)
4. takeown /F <path>\maintenanceservice.exe
5. Replace binary with malicious executable (reverse shell)
6. sc.exe start MozillaMaintenance → SYSTEM code execution

PATCH STATUS: Patched in March 2020 updates. Not viable on patched systems.
Alternatives on unpatched: CVE-2018-0952, CVE-2019-0841

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Hyper-V Admin → DC clone → NTDS.dit offline → krbtgt hash → Golden Ticket (unlimited persistence)
DC clone: minimal forensic evidence (only Hyper-V snapshot activity logs)
Hard link → Mozilla service → SYSTEM → secretsdump local hashes → lateral movement
NTDS.dit dump from cloned DC → same attack as Backup Operators path → all domain hashes

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Hyper-V Administrators group membership = treat as Domain Admin in virtualized environments
Infrastructure/server teams commonly granted this role — frequently overlooked
Hyper-V hosts with DC VMs = highest value target in entire environment
name: Hyper-V Administrators - Service Binary Hijack
description: Hyper-V Administrators effectively have SYSTEM-level file access. Take ownership of a SYSTEM-run service binary (e.g. Mozilla Maintenance Service), replace it with a payload, and start the service. CVE-2018-0952 / CVE-2019-0841 symlink abuse is the classic path.

defense.why_it_works: Hyper-V Administrators have full control over Hyper-V, including live virtual machines. If the Domain Controller runs as a Hyper-V guest, a Hyper-V Admin can access the VM's virtual disk, memory dump, or use the Hyper-V Manager to extract credentials. Additionally, CVE-2018-0952 and CVE-2019-0841 can be exploited by Hyper-V Admins to take ownership of SYSTEM-owned files and replace them with malicious binaries that execute as SYSTEM.
defense.prerequisites: Membership in the Hyper-V Administrators group. For file ownership exploit: Windows 10/Server 2016+ with unpatched CVE-2018-0952 or CVE-2019-0841. For DC compromise: DC running as a Hyper-V guest on the attacker's accessible host.
defense.impact: Full control over Hyper-V VMs including pausing, exporting, and accessing virtual machine disk files. If DC is a guest, equivalent to Domain Admin. Alternatively, SYSTEM-level code execution on the Hyper-V host via exploit chains.
defense.detection: Hyper-V event log: VM exported or connected to by Hyper-V Admin. takeown executed on SYSTEM-owned files by Hyper-V Admin. Unexpected Hyper-V management operations during off-hours.
defense.artifacts: Hyper-V event log (VM export/access) | Audit log: takeown on SYSTEM files | Process: Hyper-V management by non-admin account
defense.prevention: Treat Hyper-V Administrators as equivalent to Domain Admin — restrict membership strictly. If DCs are virtualized, segregate their Hyper-V host access. Apply patches for CVE-2018-0952 and CVE-2019-0841. Monitor Hyper-V admin activities with enhanced auditing.
defense.misconfiguration: Regular users or developers added to Hyper-V Administrators group without understanding escalation implications. Domain Controllers running as Hyper-V guests on hosts accessible to Hyper-V Admins.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# User in Hyper-V Administrators
net localgroup 'Hyper-V Administrators'

# Exploit: takeown on SYSTEM-protected file
takeown /F 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Mozilla Maintenance Service\maintenanceservice.exe'
# Then replace with malicious binary and start service
defense.secure_config:
# Audit Hyper-V Administrators
net localgroup 'Hyper-V Administrators'

# Remove unnecessary members
# Apply security updates for CVE-2018-0952 and CVE-2019-0841
# Segregate DC virtual infrastructure — dedicated Hyper-V hosts with separate admin accounts
# Enhanced auditing on Hyper-V host operations
